messages:
Emma (PM): FYI -- ZephyrHealth reported sustained throughput drop and p95 spikes after our last model rollout. They just pinged sales and support; asking for triage + product prioritization.
Liam (Support): Customer reported from their end at 08:12 UTC: requests/kitchen route returning 503s and long tail latency. They attached sample request IDs.
Rachel (Sales): Zephyr is on a renewed contract; they're sensitive to SLA (monthly credits if >2% errors). They're asking for ETA on fix.
Devon (Eng Runtime): Can you paste the request IDs and model version? Need to check routing and overflow to fallback.
Liam (Support): Sample IDs: r-8f3a2, r-8f3a7, r-8f3bb. Model: gpt-redwood-13b-v2. Rolled out at 2026-03-03 22:00 UTC per deploy-bot.
ops-bot: deploy finished: gpt-redwood-13b-v2 @ canary -> prod at 2026-03-03T22:03:14Z
Priya (Oncall): Looking at metrics: on route /api/v1/generate/kitchen p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~820ms starting 2026-03-04 01:05 UTC. QPS dropped ~38% at the same time.
Samir (Eng Platform): Any config changes to batching or kv-cache? We had a subtle default KV cache TTL change in the last infra patch.
Devon (Eng Runtime): We did change adaptive batching defaults (max_batch_size bumped to 64) in that rollout. That could increase queueing for short requests.
Emma (PM): Customer-facing ask: they need either a rollback option or a mitigation (dedicated capacity or route priority). Which is fastest?
Rachel (Sales): Zephyr prefers no rollback if we can offer temporary dedicated pool and SLA credit until fixed. They want timeline ASAP.
Priya (Oncall): For immediate mitigation, we can route Zephyr to a legacy model variant (gpt-redwood-13b-v1) via per-customer routing rule. That avoids infra rollback. I can push that rule once approved.
Devon (Eng Runtime): Agree. But we should verify that v1 handles same load without increased cost. Also need to confirm session KV compatibility.
Liam (Support): Customer ok with variant, requested that we keep it for 48h and monitor.
Emma (PM): Product decision needed: do we triage this as P0 bug (rollback-worthy) or P1 incident (mitigate + backlog fix)? Consider customer revenue and SLA.
Samir (Eng Platform): From infra POV, the KV TTL change + adaptive batching combo looks suspicious. If adaptive batching changed server-side default, it could increase head-of-line blocking for short responses, hurting p95. That needs a code change or config rollback.
Devon (Eng Runtime): I can reproduce a similar p95 increase in staging by setting max_batch_size=64 and send short prompts. Confirmed head-of-line queueing at 500-700ms.
Priya (Oncall): Repro steps (staging):
```
# flood short prompts
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-13b-v2","prompt":"x"}' & done
```
Observe p95 jump when max_batch_size >= 48.
Devon (Eng Runtime): Root cause hypothesis: adaptive batching change + different kernel scheduling for v2 increases per-batch latency for short seqs.
Emma (PM): Acceptance criteria if we treat as Product backlog item: 1) Reproduce in staging; 2) Fix or config rollback that restores p95 < 250ms for short requests; 3) Document mitigation & add guardrails to rollout checklist; 4) Customer comms and temporary routing applied.
Rachel (Sales): If we commit to that, Zephyr will accept the temporary variant and formal fix in next sprint. They asked for weekly updates.
Liam (Support): I applied the per-customer routing to v1 for Zephyr at 09:47 UTC and notified them. Noted no immediate errors now, but still watching.
ops-bot: routing-rule applied: customer=zephyrhealth -> model=gpt-redwood-13b-v1 at 2026-03-04T09:47:22Z
Priya (Oncall): Action items I propose: (1) Devon to produce a short patch or pin adaptive batching default; (2) Samir to audit infra default changes and add rollout guard; (3) Emma to file a product bug and prioritize in sprint; (4) Support to maintain temporary routing + customer comms.
Devon (Eng Runtime): I can push a hotfix to pin max_batch_size=32 for v2 canary and prod override within 2-4 hours. Need ownership from Platform for config rollout.
Samir (Eng Platform): I'll approve a platform-level feature-flag change for the default. Will coordinate safe rollout window.
Emma (PM): For backlog entry: I'll create a ticket with the acceptance criteria above and mark as P0 for this week with owner Devon + Platform. We'll negotiate scope: long-term fix could be kernel-level scheduling improvements vs conservative defaults. Document both options.
Liam (Support): Customer notified: "we've applied a temporary routing and are working on a fix; we'll update in 24h." They responded :relieved:.
Rachel (Sales): Logging this in CRM and am scheduling a commercial check-in for Friday.
Devon (Eng Runtime): Quick note: to help root cause, please attach perf traces (tracing IDs) for sample requests r-8f3a2 etc. I pulled partial logs but need full span traces.
Liam (Support): Pasted trace IDs into the ticket.
Emma (PM): OK team — summary & next steps: 1) mitigation applied (routing to v1); 2) Devon/Samir to pin default and test in staging; 3) Emma to file product ticket with acceptance criteria and customer timeline; 4) Support to keep customer updated. We'll reconvene in 6h or sooner if regressions continue.
Priya (Oncall): I'm keeping an eye on p95/throughput dashboards and will alert if >10% deviation.
Devon (Eng Runtime): Starting patch now, will report ETA in thread.
Samir (Eng Platform): I'll prepare config rollout plan and rollback steps.
Emma (PM): Thanks everyone. Marking thread as actionable.
Rachel (Sales): Thanks — customer appreciated the fast response.
Emma (PM): (adds) Also let's add a roadmap item to improve rollout checklist and add canary traffic shape tests for short prompt workloads.
